summary.headline: Triveni Q1 FY27 revenue rose 2% YoY to ₹1,581 crore and PBT turned positive at ₹5 crore (vs ₹9 crore loss), led by sugar and distillery margins.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 is the first quarter after the power transmission business was demerged into Triveni Power Transmission Ltd (effective 1 April 2026; scheme effective 19 May 2026), so figures are for continuing operations with prior periods restated. Revenue grew 2% YoY to ₹1,581 crore and EBITDA rose 6%, with sugar margins and distillery PBIT (up 32%) doing most of the work. Water revenue fell 21% on slower Prayagraj and Vadodara EPC execution. Management said the quarter was better than its own expectations and flagged improving sugar prices and a stock-limit order from the government for Aug–Nov 2026.

segments.name: Sugar
segments.commentary: Domestic dispatches up 7% and realisation up 3% YoY; segment revenue ₹1,235 crore and PBIT ₹14 crore (+82%). Sugar inventory at 30 June 2026 was 3.59 lakh MT at ₹38.41/kg versus 4.45 lakh MT a year earlier.

segments.name: Alcohol / Distillery
segments.commentary: Production 57,488 KL (-12% YoY) and sales 50,483 KL (-19% YoY) on lower sales orders; grain-based share of alcohol sales rose to 61% from 58%. PBIT ₹31 crore (+32%) on lower maize costs, better DDGS realisation and efficiencies.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹43 crore (-21%); orders received ₹9 crore in the quarter; closing order book ₹1,472 crore, including ₹1,065 crore of long-duration O&M. Bids in the quarter exceeded ₹300 crore.

segments.name: Country liquor / branded alcohol
segments.commentary: Country liquor volumes about 15.5 lakh cases, marginally down on a UP excise quota revision. Branded spirits are launched in UP and Delhi and are not yet profitable per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a significantly better operating season in FY27 (sugar season 2026-27) for Triveni's cost economics, led by a rebound at Shamli and CapEx benefits at the other seven sugar units.
Management expects a good Q2 on the back of sugar price strength.

Sugar: management sees 'excellent' sugar pricing ahead, with pricing expected to hold at current levels; domestic sugar consumption estimated at 28.3 MT by Triveni versus government estimate of 28.1 MT.

Ethanol: management estimates next-year (ESY 2026-27) ethanol procurement of about 1,300 crore litres and expects a roughly 3:1 grain-to-sugary feedstock ratio; expects Triveni to match that mix via multi-feed distilleries.
Water: management expects to achieve the year's operating plan, though execution is lumpy; recent tenders are under pursuit.
Management said there is sufficient country-liquor capacity for at least the next three quarters.
capex_capacity: Sugar crush for 2025-26 was 8.25 million MT, down about 9% YoY on poorer yields and higher diversion; gross recovery improved 26 bps to 11.1%.
Sir Shadi Lal (Shamli) crushed 82 lakh quintals at 10.4% recovery in FY26; management expects a higher number of operating days, lower diversion and better recovery in 2026-27.
Some CapEx has gone into sugar plant cost efficiency (steam economics, bagasse savings) for the upcoming season.
Management will maximise crystallisation capacity for sugar next year rather than divert juice to ethanol in UP.
Capital allocation review is under active examination by the board; management said water needs better ROCE before more capital, and country liquor needs little capital but is capped by UP geography.
demand_pricing: Sugar prices: refined sugar about ₹4,600/quintal and sulphitation sugar about ₹4,525/quintal as of the call date, versus the previous-quarter average.
Government order effective 1 Aug–30 Nov 2026 caps dealer stock holdings at 4,000 quintals and 30 days.
Industry closing stock for 2025-26 estimated at about 4 MT, the lowest since Sept 2017 (3.88 MT).
Sugar cane price (SAP) hike last season was ₹30/quintal, the highest ever; management is uncertain about SAP for the next season given UP elections in early 2027.

Maize prices rose in the single-digit percentage range over four to five months; DDGS realisation offsets the maize rise. MP maize procurement expected from November; current maize is covered until Oct–Nov.
Country liquor is a competitive market; Triveni claims top-five position in UP. Branded spirits (about 5-6% of volume) are growing but unprofitable.

Ethanol: Supreme Court has ordered status quo on existing allocation framework; AG has proposed allocation of 100 crore litres to be divided among about 200 bidders, with a hearing expected early the following week.

qa_highlights.question: Expected sugarcane yields going forward after the lower 2025-26 crush?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 2025-26 output fell about 9% on poorer yields and higher diversion, partly offset by higher recoveries. For 2026-27 it reported pest and disease incidence well below monitoring lines and adequate rainfall at five of eight factories, while stressing the next six weeks of grand growth are critical.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bottlenecks in the water business execution (Prayagraj etc.) and how will they be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Suresh Taneja called the slippage part of the business's lumpy execution and said the company should still achieve the full-year operating plan.

qa_highlights.question: How will Maharashtra and Karnataka cane output and national sugar balance look?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a flattish performance in Maharashtra and Karnataka, with limited upside. It estimates FY27 domestic consumption at 28.3 MT against the government's 28.1 MT, and says sugar supply is sufficient.

qa_highlights.question: Will mills divert more cane juice or B-heavy to ethanol and cut sugar output, and what diversion is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Triveni will maximise crystallisation capacity in UP next year. Diversion is expected to be between zero and 3 MT, with B-heavy likely to be diverted and juice diversion uncertain until October 2026 cane estimates.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ethanol offtake fall, and will capacity utilisation stay below 70%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ethanol procurement was above 1,100 crore litres this year and expects about 1,300 crore litres next year. It expects standalone distilleries running at 20-50% utilisation to face viability pressure once interest moratoriums end, so utilisation will vary by group and multi-feed capacity matters.

qa_highlights.question: Maize price outlook and cost cover?
qa_highlights.answer: Maize prices rose in the single-digit percentage range over four to five months, offset by higher DDGS realisation. Procurement covers until October-November, and MP maize is expected from November.

qa_highlights.question: Sir Shadi Lal standalone numbers and recovery outlook; debt and capital allocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Sir Shadi Lal is amalgamated, so separate EBITDA and PAT are not disclosed. FY26 crush was 82 lakh quintals at 10.4% recovery, with a rebound expected in 2026-27. Working capital borrowings are expected lower; the board is examining capital allocation, with water needing better ROCE and country liquor capped by UP geography.

risks_watch: Monsoon and grand growth period over the next six weeks for Triveni's eight sugar units, particularly Rani Nangal and Sabitgarh with lower rainfall, and El Nino risk to cane yields and recoveries.
Ethanol policy: Supreme Court status quo on allocation, AG proposal for 100 crore litres split among about 200 bidders with an early-next-week hearing, and OMC tender outcomes for ESY 2026-27.
UP cane price (SAP) decision ahead of the early-2027 UP elections, given the record ₹30/quintal hike last season and existing arrears.
Government stock limits (4,000 quintals, 30 days) for 1 Aug–30 Nov 2026 and any further intervention if prices rise.
Water execution lumpiness: revenue fell 21% and the order book of ₹1,472 crore must convert; watch the L1 wins from over ₹300 crore of bids.

Branded spirits remain unprofitable; country liquor is hit by UP excise quota revisions and penalty changes. TPTL listing expected in four to six weeks, subject to approvals, with figures not yet disclosed.
key_quotes: Our first quarter performance reflects improved operating performance in the sugar and distillery businesses, leading to an improvement in the profitability despite a challenging backdrop of lower cane yields, higher sugarcane costs, and evolving ethanol demand, and of course, slower revenue conversion in the water business.
So, we see excellent sugar pricing if one has to look at it going forward.
I think this quarter under review was a very good, if anything, better than our own expectations.
As far as the country liquor business is concerned, which is a profitable business, we're doing very well.
The water business is a... it is an excellent business. However, the return on capital employed in that business is not ideal.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on sugar pricing, the crop outlook and the FY27 operating season, and described Q1 as better than its own expectations. It was guarded on SAP, ethanol policy and the next-year capital allocation, and declined to give TPTL segment details, Sir Shadi Lal separate financials or the branded spirits numbers.

growth.why: Management guides to a significantly better FY27 sugar operating season (Shamli rebound, CapEx benefits at seven other units) and a good Q2 on sugar price strength, with working capital borrowings expected lower; no capacity addition quantified and no revenue growth number given, so backing is partial.
